influences.name: Alex Ligertwood
influences.context: Santana's been a favorite of mine since the early '80's, thanks to my Nigerian then-boyfriend who used to play Santana day and night. He was especially impressed with the vocalists; his opinion was that anyone who wanted to be a singer in that band had to have a powerful enough voice to cut through the screaming guitars! His favorite Santana singers were Alex Ligertwood and Greg Walker, and they became mine too

influences.name: Greg Walker
influences.context: His favorite Santana singers were Alex Ligertwood and Greg Walker, and they became mine too as I got more into Santana and filled my shelves with many Santana albums throughout the '80s.

influences.name: Santana
influences.context: I want Santana grooves with The Sword breakdowns thrown in.

influences.name: Jimi Hendrix
influences.context: What bands or artists influenced you to pick up an instrument and to become a musician. JIMI FREAKIN HENDRIX

influences.name: Aretha Franklin
influences.context: I remember clearly the moment that I discovered, with clarity, that I could memorize an entire album. All the parts. The bass part, the drum part, the guitar part, the voice part. And that was Aretha Franklin's Lady Soul.

influences.name: Marvin Gaye
influences.context: And, to this day, I listen to that one and Marvin Gaye's What's Going On a lot. So I learned how to play guitar around Aretha's voice, or Marvin Gaye, or Dionne Warwick.

influences.name: Dionne Warwick
influences.context: So I learned how to play guitar around Aretha's voice, or Marvin Gaye, or Dionne Warwick.

influences.name: Nina Simone
influences.context: I come from Nina Simone, Tina Turner, and Etta James – those are the ladies that I grew up with.

influences.name: Tina Turner

influences.name: Billie Holiday
influences.context: But my main queen is Billie Holiday. And I try to phrase like her a lot, her and Aretha.

influences.name: Miles Davis
influences.context: I listen mostly to women singers and guitar players because I want to think like a female singer or a Miles Davis trumpet.

influences.name: Bob Marley
influences.context: Like Bob Marley says, music helps you and I remember our totality.

influences.name: Gábor Szabó
influences.context: Yes, it started with a line that I took from my friend Gábor Szabó. And the line goes: [sings] do-dah-di-da-doo-do-dah-dah-do.

influences.name: Carlos Santana
influences.context: My father used to sit me down on his lap, like I will do with my son eventually. He would control the kick and would give me the sticks and I would just mess around with the cymbals and those types of things. My father really wanted me to learn the drums.

influences.name: Stevie Wonder
influences.context: A classic example is Stevie Wonder on Superstition playing the clavinet part. It is a very percussive sound.

influences.name: Herbie Hancock
influences.context: Off the top of my head, hands down, first and foremost, first and last, a dream come true would be working with a cat like Herbie Hancock. I mirrored my entire career after all the dope stuff that he's done; constantly not afraid to reinvent himself.

influences.name: Jay-Z
influences.context: I was vibing almost like Jay-Z and Timbaland working on the Black Album. Where Jay-Z was listening to Timbaland playing him Dirt Off Your Shoulder, this one track totally popped out at me.

influences.name: Timbaland
influences.context: I was vibing almost like Jay-Z and Timbaland working on the Black Album.
